title: Day2 KVCache + Attention Kernel Seqlen Bisect Log
content:
Context:
I continued the bisect on the KV cache / attention kernel interaction after yesterday's flaky repro. Goal: find the smallest sequence length or code path that triggers cache corruption / wrong-attention selection (observed as repeated tokens and index-out-of-range crashes in serving runtime).

Summary of reproducible symptom:
- Model: rwd-open-13b-qat (quantized v2) running on dedicated pool (A100s) local dev env
- Symptom: at certain request seqlen combinations (prompt + suffix) the response repeats the same token 2-4 times then diverges; sometimes we get fatal: "InvalidArgumentError: kv_index >= cache_size (attn_kv_cache.cc:214)"
- Failure window seems tied to near-power-of-two sequence lengths (e.g., 1023->1024 boundary, 2047->2048) and when causal cache reuse + prefix caching is enabled.

What I tried today (chronological):
1) Re-run minimal repro script (scripts/repro_seqlen_kvcache.py) with logging turned on
- cmd: python repro_seqlen_kvcache.py --model rwd-open-13b-qat --prefix-file tests/prefixes/short_prompt.txt --suffix-length 300 --enable-kvcache --cache-mode prefix
- note: same seed (42) each run for determinism
- outcome: 4/10 runs produced repeated-token behavior, 2/10 hits produced crash with InvalidArgumentError. Non-deterministic but higher probability near lengths 1022-1030.

2) Disabled prefix caching only (runtime flag: --cache-prefix false)
- cmd change only: --cache-prefix false
- outcome: No crashes across 20 runs, occasional repeated token (1/20). Hypothesis: prefix caching + KV indices offset calculation is implicated.

3) Force different attention kernel selection via env var ATTN_KERNEL_OVERRIDE (valid values: flash, causal, fallback)
- tried ATTN_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=flash / causal / fallback by exporting env then restarting runtime worker
- notes: flash shows performance gains but higher chance of repeat/crash in presence of quantized weights; causal kernel more stable but slower.
- outcome: With ATTN_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=causal, crashes disappear across 30 runs, repeats reduced to 1/30. With flash, crash rate increased slightly compared to default (default is auto-select).

4) Inspect kernel selection logic near seqlen thresholds (serving-runtime/src/kernel_selector.cc)
- found threshold table: flash preferred when seq_len <= 1024 and model type = transformer-xx
- suspicion: inclusive/exclusive off-by-one when we compute effective_seq = prompt_len + requested_len - 1 (we had different code paths doing +/-1).

5) Verbose KV cache dump at runtime for failing request
- insert debug dump in kv_cache.cc: dump buffer pointers, head/tail indices, computed kv_index for each token step to /tmp/kvdump.log
- reproduced crash and captured log. Key snippet:
  [kvdump] step=285 computed_kv_idx=1023 cache_size=1024 head=0 tail=1023
  [kvdump] step=286 computed_kv_idx=1024 cache_size=1024 head=0 tail=1023
  Fatal: InvalidArgumentError: kv_index >= cache_size at kv_cache.cc:214
- interpretation: computed_kv_idx is allowed to == cache_size in one code path which then is used to index array (0..cache_size-1). Off-by-one in computed index.

6) Reproduced in unit tests (serving-runtime/tests/test_kv_cache.py) by creating prefix length 1023 and appending tokens to reach 1024+
- test revealed two code paths for index computation: one for append_from_prefix() and one for append_from_generation(). They used different formulas for wrap-around. append_from_prefix used (head + offset) % cache_size; append_from_generation used head + offset and only mod when >= cache_size. A missing >= check in one branch caused the bug when offset == cache_size.

7) Quick patch (local) to normalize index computation to always modulo by cache_size. Created branch: local/bugfix/kvcache-index-mod. Ran unit tests.
- git checkout -b local/bugfix/kvcache-index-mod
- edit kv_cache.cc to use safe_index = (head + relative_pos) % cache_size everywhere
- ran tests: serving-runtime/tests/*: unit tests pass, but regression tests (integration) fail intermittently in quantized path under flash kernel.

8) Bisecting attention kernel interaction: comment out early return that marks kernel as compatible with quantized weights if model has qat flag. This forced selection to causal kernel in auto mode; crashes went away. Means flash+quantization combination likely exposes another issue (maybe kernel writes to kv cache differently).

Error snippets collected:
- InvalidArgumentError: kv_index >= cache_size (attn_kv_cache.cc:214)
- RuntimeError: attention_kernel_flash: unexpected stride mismatch (attn_kernels.cc:88)
- WARNING: quantized-kernel: using packed-weights-legacy path (quantize/loader.cc:47)
- stack: serving-runtime/worker.cc:301 -> attn_kernels.cc:122 -> kv_cache.cc:210

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Primary: Off-by-one index calc in one append path (confirmed) plus a missing defensive check leading to out-of-range access. Patch improves but doesn't fully fix instability under flash+quant.
B) Secondary: Flash attention kernel and quantized weight loader have slightly different assumptions about KV layout (stride, padding). When combined with the cache wrap-around, flash kernel writes/read steps misalign causing repeat tokens.
C) Tertiary: Sequence length thresholds in kernel selector produce different tiling or chunking strategies; near power-of-two boundaries tiling introduces a case where computed relative_pos equals cache_size momentarily.

Experiment matrix planned (next):
- E1: Add assert checks to detect any kv index >= cache_size earlier and NOP instead of crash (to collect metrics). Roll out in dev staging and collect # occurrences.
- E2: Add explicit unit tests for flash kernel + qat model + prefix lengths at boundary values (1022,1023,1024,1025,2047,2048) and run 200 iterations each.
- E3: Add additional logging in attn kernel for read/write offsets when quantized loader used. Compare to causal kernel logs to find mismatch.
- E4: Try changing kernel selector threshold: force flash only up to 1016 and observe failure rate. This will tell if tiling threshold interplay is the cause.

Notes to self (practical):
- If you push any hotpatch, keep it behind feature-flag kvcache-safe-index and disable by default (we need reproducible baseline).
- Get Priya to run experiments on dedicated pool during off-hours (cost) — she has the credentials.
- Add a temporary metric: runtime.kv_index_oob.count with tags {kernel, model, seqlen_bucket}.

Quick reproduction commands (local):
- python -u scripts/repro_seqlen_kvcache.py --model rwd-open-13b-qat --prefix-file tests/prefixes/edge1023.txt --suffix-length 400 --enable-kvcache --cache-mode prefix 
- ATTN_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=auto ./bin/serving-worker --config dev-config.yaml 2>&1 | tee /tmp/serving_worker.log
- Grep for kvdump: tail -n 200 /tmp/kvdump.log | sed -n '1,200p'

Patch branch notes:
- branch: local/bugfix/kvcache-index-mod (WIP)
- commit: 6b2f4a9 (local) "normalize kv index computations across append paths"
- failing tests: integration/quantized/flash_integration_test (intermittent) -> need attn kernel logging first

Immediate next steps (this afternoon):
- Add logging to attn_kernels.cc to print read/write offsets when quantized loader used (low-overhead, sampling 1/200 requests)
- Push kvcache-safe-index behind feature flag to staging and run E1 for 6 hours; collect metrics
- Run E2 unit-suite with ATTN_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=flash and causal to compare behavior
- Pair with Priya on kernel selector thresholds (she has context for the table)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there any existing contract doc for kv cache index range semantics? (I couldn't find a clear one in repo; add to design doc if none.)
- Does flash kernel assume contiguous KV layout with no wrap-around? (ask kernel authors: @jonah)
- Could packing/quantization introduce extra padding tokens that change offset arithmetic? (look into quantize/loader packing code)

Notes for future PR description (if/when we commit):
- explain root cause: inconsistent index math across append code paths causing occasional kv_index == cache_size -> out-of-range; add normalized mod and guard checks; add logging and feature-flag; follow-up to investigate flash+quant path mismatch

Random scribbles:
- observed repeat pattern: token sequence A B B B C (B repeated 3x) -- looks like kernel read duplicated a slice of KV memory rather than generating new tokens
- reproducer file: tests/prefixes/edge1023.txt (contains multi-sentence prompt + trailing newline)

If I can't find kernel mismatch quickly, fallback: force kernel selector to pick causal for quantized models until we trace it. Not ideal for perf but safe for customers.

-- Aisha
